title.en: Plural nouns, singular nouns and noun + noun
title.es: Plurales, singulares engañosos y noun + noun

summary.en: Some nouns look singular but take a **plural verb** (_the police_, _people_), some end in **-s** but take a **singular verb** (_economics_, _news_), and some exist only in the plural (_trousers_, _glasses_, _scissors_). To combine two nouns, put the **describing noun first and keep it singular**: _a shoe shop_, _a train ticket_, _a ten-minute walk_.
summary.es: Tres trampas frecuentes: _the police are_ (plural) aunque en español es «la policía es»; _mathematics is_ (singular) aunque en español es «las matemáticas son»; y _a ten-minute walk_, sin -s en _minute_.

form: **Always plural**, with a plural verb: _police, people, clothes, cattle_
**Only plural** (two parts): _trousers, jeans, glasses, scissors, pyjamas_ → use _a pair of_ to count them
**Look plural, take a singular verb**: _news, economics, mathematics, physics, athletics_
**Irregular plurals**: _man → men, woman → women, child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, mouse → mice, criterion → criteria, phenomenon → phenomena_
**Group nouns** (_team, family, government, staff_): singular or plural verb in British English, depending on whether we think of one unit or of its members
**Noun + noun**: first noun singular, working like an adjective: _a bus driver_, _a language school_. With numbers use hyphens and no -s: _a three-day course_
A few first nouns keep their **-s**: _a clothes shop_, _a sports centre_, _a savings account_, _the accounts department_

uses.text: **Police, people, staff**: _The police **have** arrested two men. A lot of people **were** waiting outside._
**Two-part objects**: _My trousers **are** too long. Where **are** my glasses? I need a new **pair of** jeans._
**Subjects in -s**: _Economics **is** a popular degree. The news **was** a surprise._
**Group nouns**: _My family **are** all coming to the wedding._ (the people) _The family **is** the most important unit in society._ (the group as a whole)

note.en: In American English the singular verb is more usual with group nouns; both are correct in British English.
note.es: En inglés británico valen ambos; el singular es más habitual en inglés americano.

uses.text: **Measurements in a noun phrase**: _a ten-minute walk_, _a five-pound note_, _a two-hour delay_. But the same thing as a predicate takes -s: _The walk is ten minutes._

why.en: Trousers is always plural, so it takes a plural verb.
why.es: En español «mi pantalón es», pero _trousers_ es siempre plural: _are_.

mistakes.wrong: The police is investigating the case.
mistakes.right: The police are investigating the case.

why.en: Police is always followed by a plural verb.
why.es: _The police_ lleva siempre verbo en plural.
Las asignaturas en -ics (_mathematics, physics, economics_) llevan verbo en singular.

why.en: A noun used as an adjective stays singular, even after a number.
why.es: Con un número delante, el sustantivo-adjetivo no lleva -s: _a two-week holiday_.

mistakes.wrong: She works in a shoes shop.
mistakes.right: She works in a shoe shop.

why.en: The first noun in a noun + noun combination is normally singular.
why.es: El primer sustantivo va en singular: _shoe shop_ (como «zapatería»).

examples.en: My trousers are too long; could you shorten them?
examples.es: Los pantalones me quedan largos; ¿podrías acortarlos?

examples.en: Do you have a pair of scissors I could borrow?
The police have asked drivers to avoid the city centre.
examples.es: La policía ha pedido a los conductores que eviten el centro.

examples.en: Physics was my favourite subject at school.
My family are all coming to the wedding.
Three women and two men applied for the post.
The criteria for the scholarship are very strict.
I've booked a two-week course in Dublin.
examples.es: He reservado un curso de dos semanas en Dublín.

examples.en: She works in a clothes shop, and her brother is a bus driver.
There's a ten-minute walk from the station to the campus.

practice.prompt: The police ___ asked everyone to stay indoors.

explanation.en: Police is always plural, so it takes have.

practice.prompt: Where ___ my glasses? I can't find them anywhere.

explanation.en: Glasses is a plural noun and takes are.

practice.prompt: It's a ___ walk from the hotel to the beach.

explanation.en: In a noun phrase before another noun, minute stays singular and is joined to the number with a hyphen.

practice.prompt: Economics ___ one of the most popular degrees at our university.

explanation.en: Names of subjects ending in -ics are singular.

practice.prompt: There's a lovely ___ shop in the old town.

explanation.en: The first noun in noun + noun is singular: a shoe shop.
